sentences.text: Sinocalliopteryx was a carnivorous theropod dinosaur that walked on two legs.
The original 2007 specimen was the largest known member of the Compsognathidae family, measuring 2.37 meters in length.
Its skull was up to 29 centimetres long and featured numerous serrated, conical teeth in the premaxillae and curved teeth in the maxillae.
Protofeathers covered the back of the skull, neck, back, hips, tail, and parts of the limbs, with the longest feathers found on the hips, the base of the tail, and the rear portions of the femur.
The holotype skeleton contained a preserved dromaeosaurid leg inside its abdominal cavity, including a tibia fragment measuring 15.5 cm in length.
Remains of at least two Confuciusornis sanctus birds and a 13.5-centimetre scapula from a 1.5-metre-long herbivorous ornithischian were found in the second specimen.
The species Sinocalliopteryx gigas was first named and described in 2007 by a team of four researchers.
The holotype was excavated in Hengdaozi, Sihetun locality, Beipiao, west Liaoning province.
The original fossil specimen was found at Hengdaozi in Liaoning Province, China, and dates to about 125 million years ago.
There are two recorded fossil occurrences of Sinocalliopteryx in the Paleobiology Database.
Researchers suggested the preserved prey leg indicates Sinocalliopteryx preyed on smaller, bird-like dinosaurs, and the capture of multiple birds suggests it may have specialized in bird prey.
Sinocalliopteryx was likely a ground-dwelling predator that could catch birds using stealth attacks.
The stones in the abdomen were interpreted as gastroliths similar to those found in other theropods, though no special gizzard would have been present in Sinocalliopteryx.
The original researchers assigned Sinocalliopteryx to the family Compsognathidae, and it is classified within this group as the parent group.
Sinocalliopteryx is considered the last member of the family Compsognathidae to be discovered.
Sinocalliopteryx lived in China during the Lower Cretaceous period, approximately 124.6 million years ago, specifically during the Barremian to Aptian stages from 125.77 to 119.57 million years ago.
The flora of its habitat included conifers such as pines and araucarias.

A 2024 study by Andrea Cau questioned the classification of Sinocalliopteryx within the Compsognathidae family, while recent analyses suggest it may belong to a group called Sinosauropterygidae rather than Compsognathidae.

Recent analyses suggest Sinocalliopteryx is phylogenetically closer to Guanlong, Proceratosaurus, and Mirischia than originally thought, and it is debated whether Sinocalliopteryx and related genera should be placed within Tyrannosauroidea despite being closer to birds than tyrannosauroids.
